nodes.question: What observation is common during reef-wide bleaching and mortality events?
nodes.answer: It is common to observe certain corals appearing pigmented or healthy while others bleach or partially bleach during reef-wide bleaching and mortality events.

The symbiotic relationship between corals and dinoflagellates is vital to the success of tropical reef-building corals in the Caribbean (Hoegh-Guldberg and Smith 1989; Hughes et al. 2017; Kawamura et al. 2021). Most Caribbean corals species acquire symbiotic algae during early life from the sediment and water column (Roth 2014). Once acquired, symbionts contribute photosynthetic products to coral cells and can serve as a heterotrophic food source in nutrient-limited conditions (Nitschke et al. 2016; Roth 2014; Wiedenmann et al. 2023). The accumulation of temperature and irradiance stress can result in symbionts overproducing harmful photosynthetic by-products, driving the system toward dysbiosis.
